body:
## Problem / outcome

Deliver personal subscription-backed access with LiteLLM → CLIProxyAPI, native
personal Usage and native Langfuse content-rich debugging traces. Capture
prompts/source code sent in requests, model responses and tool contents visible
to the integration, with accurate attribution and targeted credential masking.
Reuse upstream accounts, keys, limits, reporting and telemetry; organize ProxyLens
work around configuration and demonstrated integration gaps.

## Revision and current state

Revised in place on October 29, 2026 with owner approval. Original issue bodies are archived in
`docs/planning/archive/issues-before-2026-10-29.json`. Existing code implements
Keycloak/group/custom-gateway contracts; its evidence is preserved, not relabeled.
ADR 0002 remains proposed until the candidate is accepted. Later on October 29,
the owner approved useful native Langfuse content capture, superseding the earlier
metadata-only candidate objective and blanket content-removal callback proposal.

## Scope

- Own the shared scope in `docs/specs/litellm-poc.md` and record choices needed by
  setup: actual client/model, native edition, ordinary role and enabled policies.
- Coordinate #2 configuration, #8 Langfuse, #7 one integration acceptance pass,
  and #6 production readiness/cutover. #5/#9 consolidate into #2; #4 into #7.
- Keep #3 optional diagnostics and #10 deferred reporting-gap work.
- Review native behavior and concrete gaps before accepting the candidate. Native
  features require no custom implementation or repeated upstream test suite.

## Dependencies

#2/#8 configure the candidate, #7 supplies A1–A6 evidence, #6 prepares production
readiness. Scope decisions happen first; candidate acceptance precedes separately
approved cutover. No dependency on closing optional/deferred tickets.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Required client/model, native feature scope and configuration choices are
  recorded. Additional requirements are explicit, not inferred from old contracts.
- [ ] #2/#8 deliver the configured candidate and #7 completes the shared A1–A6
  checks: native access, client protocol, ownership/usage, controls, telemetry and
  CPAMP-independent native Usage.
- [ ] Native UI gaps and observed limitations are reviewed. Wrong ownership,
  credential exposure, unauthorized trace access or broken required client
  behavior blocks acceptance; intended debugging content is not a privacy failure.
  Custom work is scoped only for an agreed gap.
- [ ] Deferred handoff P1–P13 scenarios are recorded as deferred/conditional, not
  passed. No strict-budget, lossless-accounting or exactly-once-delivery claim is
  made from a smoke check.
- [ ] Owner accepts or rejects the candidate with evidence. On acceptance, update
  ADR statuses, glossary and guidance together; authorize cutover separately in #6.

## Non-goals

Reimplementing native LiteLLM features; certifying all upstream internals; advanced
statistics, custom accounting store/exporter, mandatory CPAMP or immediate cutover.

## Operational notes

Preserve historical group ownership and old proof limitations. CPA remains the
provider/OAuth boundary; CPAMP is the only queue consumer when enabled. Langfuse
is observability, not authorization/accounting. Follow-up guarantees require their
own scoped evidence. Update `DEVELOPMENT.md` with decisions and actual results.

## References

`docs/specs/litellm-poc.md`; `docs/planning/architecture-rebaseline-2026-10-29.md`;
`docs/adr/0002-litellm-personal-usage.md`; `docs/live-acceptance.md`.
title: Native-first personal access: integration scope and candidate acceptance

body:
## Problem / outcome

Configure a reproducible LiteLLM → CPA deployment with native accounts, personal
keys, limits, persistent spend/history and native Usage. These are upstream
features to configure, not new ProxyLens services to implement.

## Revision and current state

Approved October 29, 2026 revision of the Compose foundation; absorbs native
account/key configuration from #5/#9. Original contracts are archived in
`docs/planning/archive/issues-before-2026-10-29.json`. Current `compose.yaml`
deploys Keycloak/custom services/CPA/CPAMP, not LiteLLM; preserve its runtime state.
The owner's later October 29 clarification selects native Langfuse content-rich
tracing in #8; the earlier blanket content-capture prohibition is superseded.
Recorded startup privacy settings are current configuration, not the new objective.

## Scope

- Isolated candidate Compose/config, LiteLLM database, CPA inference route,
  necessary coordination dependencies, secrets and native UI ingress.
- Pin the actual image/digest, schema and configuration; record the chosen
  edition. The research snapshot is not an installed-image guarantee.
- Configure native onboarding and ordinary-user role, users A/B, personal keys
  (including a second key for A), allowed models and selected native limits.
- Enable native persisted usage/Usage UI; set explicit CPA alias pricing where
  needed. Keep native accounting separate from #8's content-rich Langfuse
  debugging traces; #8 records required native logging options and targeted
  credential masking. No new ledger or dashboard backend.
- Supply native secret/callback configuration seams for #8 and fixture for #7.

## Dependencies

#1 actual client/model, deployment endpoints, selected policies and CPA sharing
decision. #8 owns Langfuse integration settings; #7 owns the shared behavioral
checks. #6 owns production backup/restore and cutover. No mandatory CPAMP profile.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Documented commands start the pinned candidate with persistent state,
  healthchecks and private data/management services; existing state is isolated.
- [ ] Native ordinary-user login, user-owned keys, selected model/limit policies
  and native Usage are configured in the chosen edition. Record documented native
  defaults/semantics; any paid dependency needs a visible product decision.
- [ ] Admin-created personal keys explicitly identify their intended owner; avoid
  admin-viewer roles for personal access. CPA service/admin and personal keys are
  distinct, server-side secrets are not committed or exposed to browsers.
- [ ] CPA alias prices, native logging/privacy options and storage ownership are
  recorded. Optional coordination services are included only when required.
- [ ] A startup/native-login smoke check succeeds; provide the reproducible A/B
  fixture to #7. Do not duplicate its full integration acceptance here.
- [ ] CPAMP is optional, with no second consumer of an existing CPA queue.
  Candidate setup/teardown and state-preserving rollback are documented.

## Non-goals

Custom user/key/policy services, custom reporting database or UI, native-feature
unit suites, provider OAuth replacement, HA or production cutover.

## Operational notes

Reuse CPA deployment/secrets patterns. Record exact versions/configuration and
dependency ownership in candidate deployment docs and `DEVELOPMENT.md`. Preserve
the current deployment until #6's approved cutover.

## References

`docs/specs/litellm-poc.md`; `compose.yaml`; `deploy/cliproxyapi/`;
`docs/deployment.md`; `docs/dependency-pins.md`.
title: Configure LiteLLM → CPA: deployment, native accounts, keys, limits, and Usage

body:
## Problem / outcome

Make this deployment recoverable and perform an approved cutover after candidate
acceptance. Test our state handling and migration, not all LiteLLM internals.

## Revision and current state

Approved October 29, 2026 revision. Original operations spec is archived in
`docs/planning/archive/issues-before-2026-10-29.json`. `docs/operations.md` and
`docs/deployment.md` describe the existing custom services, not native guarantees.

## Scope

- Inventory native user/key/budget/history state, CPA OAuth/configuration and
  selected telemetry/diagnostic stores; document secret and retention ownership.
  For #8's content-rich native Langfuse traces, record native project access,
  actual content-retention settings and backup/recovery ownership explicitly.
- Document and rehearse populated backup/restore and version/schema-compatible
  upgrade/rollback for the selected deployment.
- Prepare key issuance, historical-data handling, ingress switch and rollback;
  execute only after #1 candidate acceptance and separate cutover approval.
- Reuse #7 integration evidence and record native limitations. Add load benchmarks
  or accounting fault injection only for an explicit workload/guarantee.

## Dependencies

Readiness preparation begins after #2. #7/#8 supply integration/telemetry results.
#1 accepts the candidate before production cutover. #3/#10 matter only if selected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every selected state/secret has a backup and retention owner; actual retention
  values are recorded rather than inherited from old services by assumption.
- [ ] A populated restore recovers users, personal-key ownership, retained history
  and budget state; verify with a small native login/history/request check.
- [ ] Upgrade/rollback instructions identify matching binary/schema/state versions,
  incompatible migrations and how to restore the previous ingress safely.
- [ ] Health distinguishes inference, native history availability and telemetry;
  reuse #7's restart/optional-dependency checks rather than repeat a fault matrix.
- [ ] Native delivery/accounting/limit behavior and accepted limitations are
  documented. Stronger guarantees need explicit scope and supporting tests.
- [ ] Cutover plan issues replacement keys where required, preserves old group
  history or separates the accounting epoch, defines rollback triggers and keeps
  recoverable old state. Do not infer personal owners from old key creators.
- [ ] After owner approval, execute cutover and repeat the small essential client,
  login/usage and telemetry checks; retire superseded services only after success.

## Non-goals

HA, broad upstream crash-loss/overshoot certification, capacity benchmarks without
a target workload, silent state deletion, or production-request replay.

## Operational notes

The proposed 90/365/90-day retention values are starting options, not upstream
defaults. Optional CPAMP remains the sole queue consumer. The owner's later
October 29 clarification approves native Langfuse content-rich debugging traces,
superseding the metadata-only candidate objective. Record the selected content
retention and trace-viewing access without treating userId filters as authorization;
keep credentials excluded through targeted handling. Update deployment docs and
`DEVELOPMENT.md` with tested restore commands, accepted limits and cutover results.

## References

`docs/specs/litellm-poc.md`; `docs/operations.md`; `docs/deployment.md`.
title: Production readiness: backup, restore, and controlled cutover

body:
## Problem / outcome

Verify our configured LiteLLM → CPA → native Usage/Langfuse integration with one
small end-to-end fixture. Native features are reused; this checks configuration,
provider compatibility and trusted mappings rather than retesting LiteLLM itself.

## Revision and current state

Approved October 29, 2026 revision; absorbs usage verification from #4 and shared
account/key/UI checks. Original gateway issue is archived in
`docs/planning/archive/issues-before-2026-10-29.json`. Existing gateway tests and
`scripts/live-acceptance.py` supply reusable scenarios, not candidate pass evidence.

## Scope

Run shared plan A1–A6 with users A/B, a second personal key for A, one service-owned
CPA key, actual client/version and a separate Langfuse test project. Share request
results across checks. Prefer a reproducible runbook; write regression tests for
our custom glue or a concrete defect, not native CRUD internals.

## Dependencies

#2 configured stack, role, keys, pricing and policies; #8 native telemetry mapping
and content-rich tracing with targeted credential masking. No mandatory CPAMP,
custom read adapter or reporting store. The owner's later October 29 clarification
supersedes the former metadata-only A5 criterion; historical results remain unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **A1:** A/B log in and see own keys/usage. A representative direct attempt to
  read B's history/detail as A is denied. Test the actual ordinary role selected.
- [ ] **A2:** Actual client works with nonstreaming/SSE Responses and tool/result
  continuation; exercise image/history/ancillary routes only when used. One upstream
  error and interrupted stream preserve behavior without partial-output replay.
- [ ] **A3:** A's keys aggregate to A and B stays separate. Compare sample response
  usage to retained native details/totals, including supplied cache/reasoning;
  missing measurements/pricing are explicit and subsets aren't double-counted.
  A completed native record survives restart.
- [ ] **A4:** One revoked-key and one model restriction denial cause no forbidden
  CPA request. Exercise a configured budget/rate limit, record native enforcement
  and propagation semantics, and avoid claiming strict concurrency guarantees.
- [ ] **A5:** The shared sample reaches Langfuse through one native integration
  with trusted owner/session attribution and useful prompts/source-code snippets,
  model outputs and tool arguments/results visible to the gateway, plus metrics
  and useful errors. Inspect actual payload/readback for expected content and
  excluded credentials, including selected tool/image/error and forged-metadata
  cases; record missing/truncated fields and native trace-viewing access. Forged
  metadata cannot impersonate another owner or redirect the configured destination.
  UserId filters are not authorization. Sink outage leaves inference usable and
  never replays provider work.
- [ ] **A6:** Healthy inference and native personal Usage work without CPAMP.
  Walk through history/native filters, record observed reporting lag and missing
  panels, and obtain baseline acceptance or a concrete gap decision in #1/#10.
- [ ] Record exact versions/config, client/route, sanitized results and limitations
  once for the run. Failures become focused integration fixes and retests.

## Non-goals

Exhaustive native endpoint/role/lifecycle testing, custom accounting infrastructure,
full crash-loss/replay or performance certification, or claiming deferred handoff
P1–P13 scenarios passed. Broaden tests for our custom behavior or a real failure.

## Operational notes

Use bounded synthetic traffic, keep secrets/content out of evidence and never
replay an ambiguous provider request to repair telemetry. #6 owns production
restore/cutover. Preserve `docs/live-acceptance.md` as historical old-path evidence.

## References

`docs/specs/litellm-poc.md` A1–A6 and handoff mapping;
`docs/live-acceptance.md`; `scripts/live-acceptance.py`.
title: Integration acceptance: actual client, personal usage, controls, and telemetry

body:
## Problem / outcome

Use LiteLLM's native Langfuse integration to give users useful debugging traces:
prompts (including source code sent in requests), model responses, tool names,
arguments/results visible to the gateway, and useful errors alongside timing,
model, supplied usage and estimated cost. Keep accurate user/session attribution
and selectively exclude credentials rather than removing application content.

## Revision and current state

Owner clarified and approved content-rich native tracing on October 29, 2026.
This supersedes the candidate's earlier metadata-only objective and proposed
blanket content-removal callback. The original custom exporter contract remains
archived in `docs/planning/archive/issues-before-2026-10-29.json`; the first
candidate revision is preserved in `issues-after-2026-10-29.json` in that directory.
`docs/exporter.md` and existing exporter tests remain old-runtime evidence.
Native telemetry is not yet enabled or accepted by this objective revision.

## Scope

- Choose and configure one supported native integration for the pinned
  LiteLLM/SDK/destination; reuse native payload construction and asynchronous delivery.
- Enable useful request/response and tool content for debugging. Capture only what
  the gateway/native integration observes; document truncation, unsupported fields,
  image handling and absent local tool spans instead of claiming complete app traces.
- Verify platform key-owner and session attribution. Caller metadata must not
  impersonate another owner; unverified conversation IDs use an owner-scoped,
  labeled fallback. Keep the selected destination/project under server control.
- Exclude authentication headers, API/OAuth/provider/management credentials and
  apply targeted masking where needed. Preserve useful content and errors; inspect
  actual payloads and document masking coverage rather than claiming universal
  secret detection in arbitrary source code or text.
- Record trace-viewing access using native project/access controls. A user/session
  filter is an analysis tool, not authorization. Coordinate content retention and
  recovery with #6.
- Prefer native configuration. Custom code is conditional on a demonstrated,
  owner-selected attribution or credential-handling gap; no preplanned filtering
  adapter, replacement exporter or durable outbox.

## Dependencies

#2 native stack/owner settings and a separate Langfuse test project. Joint
verification occurs in #7 A5 with the shared fixture, not a duplicate telemetry suite.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One compatible native integration, pinned versions and server-side project
  credentials are configured reproducibly; duplicate exporters are not enabled.
- [ ] The shared sample exposes useful prompts/source-code snippets, outputs and
  tool arguments/results that cross the gateway, plus timing/status/model/usage/cost.
  Unsupported, truncated or missing fields are recorded explicitly.
- [ ] Trusted key owner maps accurately to user attribution; forged user/session
  metadata cannot impersonate another owner. Actor, key owner, customer label and
  provider account remain distinct. Selected destination stays server-controlled.
- [ ] #7 A5 checks actual native payload/readback for expected content and credential
  exclusion, including a forged-metadata case and selected error/tool/image cases.
  Record native trace-viewing access; filters alone do not prove user isolation.
- [ ] Sink outage leaves inference usable and does not replay provider work.
  Native retry/loss/delivery limits are documented without lossless/exactly-once claims.
- [ ] Any custom hook has a demonstrated selected gap and focused regression
  tests; otherwise configuration alone completes the implementation work.

## Non-goals

Blanket metadata-only tracing, reimplementing Langfuse transport, a preplanned
outbox, broad crash/ambiguous-ack certification, automatic capture of files or local
tool activity never sent through the gateway, or Langfuse-based personal accounting.

## Operational notes

Use a separate test project and server-side secrets. Keep public implementation
evidence sanitized even though the private Langfuse project captures debugging
content. #6 records access, actual content-retention settings, credentials and
recovery ownership. Record configuration and observed limits in `DEVELOPMENT.md`.
Objective approval does not establish runtime acceptance or authorize cutover.

## References

`docs/specs/litellm-poc.md`; `docs/candidate/decisions.md`;
`docs/candidate/deployment.md`; historical `docs/exporter.md`.
title: Configure native Langfuse: content-rich debugging traces and attribution
